titleEn: Stop Right There and Call Mom!

pages.text: "Wow! A market!" Pongi called, looking at the bridge. Shops stood in a row. Mom, wearing her headscarf, held her paw tightly as they walked through the crowd. Pongi wanted to see this and that and everything.
Then a lovely smell drifted from a bread cart. "Bread! Bread!" Pongi let go and ran over. Only half of Mom's headscarf showed between the people.
After looking at the bread, Pongi turned around. Mom's place was empty. She looked around between unfamiliar feet. No headscarf anywhere. Her heart thumped, and her mouth trembled.
Pongi was close to tears. Then she remembered what Mom always said. "Stop right there and call Mom!" She was about to run into the crowd, but she planted both feet. Whew! She took a deep breath.
Pongi stood right there and called as loudly as she could. "Mom! Mom!" People turned to look. The red cord around Pongi's neck stood out brightly in the crowd.
Pongi spoke clearly to the woman beside the bread cart. "I've lost my mom." The woman nodded. "Well done. Let's wait here together." Pongi stayed right beside the cart.
Far away, a headscarf came through the crowd. Mom saw the red cord and knew it was Pongi straight away. Pongi stayed where she was and thumped her tail. "Mom, here!"
"Pongi!" "Mom!" Mom rushed over and hugged her snugly. Mom's paws patted her back. The woman at the bread cart smiled.
Mom held Pongi's paw tightly again. "One, stop right where you are! Two, call 'Mom!' loudly! Three, tell a grown-up at the nearest shop!" Pongi nodded. "I did them all!"

At home, Mom hugged Pongi tight. "You stopped and called, so I found you right away." If she loses sight of Mom, staying still and calling can help them meet again. Pongi grinned. "Stop right there and call Mom!"
